mechanism_narrative: When the Federal Funds Rate is persistently below its long-run average for at least 3 consecutive months, the S&P 500 forward 20-day return tends to be positive due to lower real borrowing costs and increased equity discounting.
failure_condition: Over a 60-day window, the 20-day forward returns are not statistically different from the mean of the pre-trigger period (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in monthly employment growth (PAYEMS) coinciding with rising consumer confidence (HOUST) predicts a positive S&P 500 20-day forward return as strong labor market expansion supports corporate earnings expectations.
failure_condition: In 20-day windows where PAYEMS growth is not accompanied by statistically significant increases in forward returns (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly decline in industrial production (INDPRO) below its prior quarter average for two consecutive months predicts a negative S&P 500 60-day forward return as it signals weakening aggregate demand and reduced corporate order backlogs.
failure_condition: Over 60 days, the 60-day forward returns are not statistically lower than the prior quarter's average (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When consumer price inflation (CPIAUCSL) unexpectedly exceeds 3% for two consecutive months, the S&P 500 20-day forward return turns negative due to market anticipation of tighter monetary policy and higher real rates.
candidate_trigger: CPIAUCSL > CPIAUCSL_prev_month + 3% AND CPIAUCSL > CPIAUCSL_prev_month + 2% for 2 consecutive months
failure_condition: In 20-day windows following such inflation spikes, forward returns are not significantly more negative than the prior 20-day average (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A rapid decline in unemployment (UNRATE) below 4.5% for three consecutive months, absent a corresponding rise in inflation (CPIAUCSL), predicts a positive S&P 500 5-day forward return as markets anticipate further easing.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE < 4.5% for 3 consecutive months AND CPIAUCSL < CPIAUCSL_prev_month + 1% over same window
regime_hint: Labor market tightening with controlled inflation
failure_condition: Over 5 days, the 5-day forward returns are not statistically positive relative to the prior 5-day window (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sudden drop in labor market participation (PAYEMS) accompanied by a sustained rise in consumer spending (HOUST) predicts a positive S&P 500 60-day forward return as it signals a shift toward a more productive working-age population.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS < PAYEMS_prev_month - 1% AND HOUST > HOUST_prev_month + 5% for 2 consecutive months
regime_hint: Labor participation decline with spending acceleration
failure_condition: Across 60 days, the 60-day forward returns are not significantly higher than the prior 60-day average (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When the monthly real GDP deflator (not directly observable but proxy via INDPRO and CPIAUCSL interaction) shows a double-dip recession pattern (two consecutive months of contraction followed by a month of expansion), the S&P 500 20-day forward return turns negative due to persistent supply-side uncertainty.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO < INDPRO_prev_month for 2 consecutive months AND INDPRO > INDPRO_prev_month_prev for the following month
failure_condition: In 20-day windows matching the trigger, forward returns are not statistically lower than baseline (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: During a sharp rise in the 10-year yield proxy (not directly observable but inferred from FEDFUNDS and market-implied rates), the S&P 500 60-day forward return turns negative as markets anticipate higher real rates and tighter credit conditions.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS > FEDFUNDS_prev_month + 0.5% for 3 consecutive months AND 10Y implied yield rises > 25 bps over same window (inferred from market data context)
failure_condition: Over 60 days post-trigger, 60-day forward returns are not significantly more negative than the prior 60-day average (t-test p > 0.05).
